Rapid Growth in the Enterprise AI Market

The year 2025 marked a period of accelerated integration of AI technologies into enterprise business processes. The enterprise AI market grew from $1.7 billion in 2023 to $37 billion, accounting for 6 percent of the SaaS market. This increase clearly demonstrates companies’ demand for generative AI and automation solutions.

Autonomous Agents and Hyperautomation

While the vast majority of companies have begun using AI in at least one business function, autonomous AI agents have emerged as the next phase of the digital workforce. Although these agents, which possess the ability to make independent decisions, are currently focused on pilot phases rather than full-scale production, they have created concrete use cases in areas such as sales and legal technology. Experts emphasize that processes must be designed to be AI-compatible from the outset, rather than simply being automated.

In back-office operations, hyperautomation—the combination of AI and robotic process automation (RPA)—has come to the fore. Automating repetitive tasks has accelerated data processing while reducing operational costs. In the physical world, the use of AI-powered robotic systems in warehouse management and on production lines has become widespread.

Infrastructure Transformation: Hybrid Cloud and Edge Computing

The increase in AI workloads has altered cloud costs and processing requirements. Companies have turned to hybrid models—combining the cloud, on-premises servers, and edge computing—to optimize costs and achieve low latency. Particularly in sectors such as finance and manufacturing that require real-time decision-making, processing data at the source has become a critical need.

2026 Outlook

By 2026, deeper human-machine collaboration and an increase in AI-powered cybersecurity measures are expected. The following topics are expected to take center stage in the tech world in the coming period:

  • The accelerated transition of autonomous systems from pilot projects to production environments.
  • Quantum computing approaching the threshold where it will outperform classical systems for certain problems.
  • The reinforcement of zero-trust architectures in cybersecurity through artificial intelligence.
  • Sustainability data being monitored as closely as financial indicators.
